doc.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 16, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Bill Crow and the union's musician programs
summary: Powell mentions Bill Crow's full-time union work and the Musician's Assistance Program seminar.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah. It can become consuming when you get involved in something.
Well for example Bill Crow, I don’t know if you know him he’s a bass player.

He’s with the union, he’s there almost full time so he doesn’t get a chance to do the traveling that I’m doing. But he’s nonetheless a fine bass player. And he’s doing his part there too. I think he’s head of some part of the union that’s doing the same thing, trying to enlighten musicians about — I think they’re called the Musician’s Assistance Program. They had a seminar, and it’s a seminar just trying to enlighten musicians to what they can do about their own plights.
